title: POC scoping - benchmark harness integration with AcmeCo
summary: Scope POC for performance benchmarking and harness integration. Agreement to run Redwood benchmark harness with AcmeCo customer scripts for representative workloads, validate streaming vs non-streaming latency/throughput, and capture cost/quality tradeoffs. Deliverables: share harness repo and runbook, customer to provide 2 workload scripts and sample dataset, joint run next week, Redwood to provide initial results and tuning recommendations.
transcript:
Header: 2026-05-14 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Alex (AE), Samir (SE), Jordan (Eng Lead - AcmeCo), Priya (SRE), Evan (ML Eng), Maya (PM)

[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda, we want to scope the POC around benchmark planning and hooking up your harness and scripts. Timebox 40 minutes.
[00:12] Jordan: Yep, super. Our goal is to validate latency at 99th pct for streaming chat and non-streaming batch generation, and get cost per 1k tokens estimates.
[00:22] Samir (SE): Great. Can you tell us the current stack? what infra, model families, and traffic patterns?
[00:31] Jordan: We're running a mix of real-time chat service and async summarization. Chat peaks at ~120 rps across 8 shards, typical message length 60 tokens, but long context up to 2k. Summarization jobs are batch, 10-15 per minute, ~1k tokens each. We use an internal orchestrator and our own KV-cache layer.
[00:49] Priya (SRE): We also have strict SLOs 150ms p50 for short chats, and 800ms p99 is our hard ceiling. Data must not leave our VPC, we prefer private deploy but will consider Redwood Dedicated for the POC.
[01:05] Samir (SE): Understood. For the bench harness integration we typically ask for: representative request scripts (user think-time and payloads), a small sample dataset for evaluation, and your load profile (rps, concurrency, arrival distribution). We'll run both streaming and non-streaming modes.
[01:25] Evan (ML Eng): For streaming vs non-streaming, I'm curious about the overhead for establishing streams. Does Redwood's streaming path keep a persistent ws or grpc stream?
[01:36] Jamie (Solutions Engineer): The hosted API supports server-sent events for stream and we also have gRPC in private/dedicated. There is some additional perp-request overhead for stream setup but we do prefix caching which helps for repeated contexts. Sometimes the transcript picks up "KV cash" instead of KV cache, so apologies if earlier docs were odd.
[01:56] Jordan: Lol ok, "KV cash" made me laugh.
[02:02] Maya (PM): Success criteria from our side: 1) p99 latency under 800ms for streaming short-turns, 2) throughput to handle 2x peak load in burst, 3) no data egress from private environment for PII workloads, and 4) quality parity vs our current model (ROUGE/BLEU style metrics and manual eval).
[02:22] Alex (AE): Good. From Redwood we propose to measure: latency distributions (p50/p95/p99), tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, and failure/error rates. We'll also run model variant fallbacks to test graceful degradation.
[02:38] Priya (SRE): On security, we need SOC2 docs, SAML SSO for console access, and audit logs shipped to our SIEM. Can you share the security pack?
[02:46] Alex (AE): Yes, we'll share the security pack and SOC2 report after the call. We'll also drop the compliance FAQ and the private deploy checklist.
[02:55] Samir (SE): Back to harness: we maintain a benchmark repo (link shared in chat) with a runner that supports both streaming and batch. We can adapt your scripts easily. Important: please give us two canonical workload scripts — one for typical chat short-turns and one for long-context summarization. Also provide environment variables for auth and endpoint info; for private deploy we'll need network access or a bastion.
[03:20] Jordan: We can provide scripts. Question: do you support byte-level streaming vs token-level? Our app does token-by-token UI rendering.
[03:30] Jamie: We stream at token boundaries and also provide chunked message streaming. There may be subtle differences across model families; we'll surface that in results.
[03:40] Evan (ML Eng): For the harness, our sampling includes corner cases: multi-turn with cache hits, cache misses for 2k contexts, and batch summarization where we feed multiple docs in a single request.
[03:52] Samir (SE): Perfect. We'll instrument the harness to record cache hit rates and measure effective tokens generated, and we can emit per-request traces so you can correlate at your side.
[04:04] Jordan: Timeline: we'd like initial numbers in a week. Is that feasible?
[04:09] Alex (AE): Yes, if we get scripts and a small dataset today or tomorrow we can spin up the runs and share initial results in ~5 business days. For private deployments there is extra lead time.
[04:19] Priya (SRE): For private, we need a checklist — network config, KMS integration, and IOPS requirements. Can you give an estimate of approximate GPU requirements for the workloads?
[04:30] Samir (SE): Rough rule of thumb: for non-quantized 7B models serving real-time chat at 120 rps with short context you'd be looking at multiple GPUs or a dedicated pool; quantized 4-bit can drastically reduce memory and increase concurrency. We'll include model/quantization recommendations per workload in the runbook.
[04:50] Maya (PM): What about measuring cost? We want per-1k token numbers including infra for dedicated.
[04:58] Alex (AE): We'll report token-level cost and also show a blended endpoint cost including infra amortization. For Dedicated we'll show a monthlyized cost per token at varying utilization levels.
[05:12] Jordan: Any caveats with streaming latencies for long contexts? My concern is that the KV cache warmup on long contexts might spike p99.
[05:21] Jamie: Yes, KV cache warmup matters; the harness will include cold-start runs and warm runs. Also we'll test prefix caching where applicable.
[05:31] Evan (ML Eng): On the technical integration, is the harness a docker-based runner? We want reproducible CI runs.
[05:38] Samir (SE): It's dockerized and we have a thin python harness. You can run locally or we can run in our infra. We'll share the repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-harness (link in chat).
[05:52] Priya (SRE): For private network testing, we need instructions for a bastion and a sample terraform module or cloudformation snippet to open a short-lived connection.
[06:02] Alex (AE): We'll provide a runbook and a sample terraform snippet.
[06:06] Jordan: Ok, let's talk measurement specifics. For streaming we want to capture first-byte latency, token-by-token timings, and end-to-end p99. For batch we want time-to-complete and throughput.
[06:18] Samir (SE): We'll export per-request events with timestamps for: request-received, stream-started, first-token, final-token, request-complete. The harness stores traces in JSONL which you can ingest.
[06:32] Maya (PM): On quality baseline, we'll run our eval set and also do a small blind A/B with 50 human evals for chat. Can you support giving us diffs vs current production model?
[06:44] Jamie: Yes, we can run the same prompts and return outputs and provide a diff report. Note there may be slight tokenization differences across runtimes.
[06:55] Evan (ML Eng): How will we compare cost/latency tradeoffs across quantized variants? We want recommendations.
[07:04] Samir (SE): We'll provide a tuning report: model family + quantization level + batch size and expected tokens/sec and cost per 1k tokens.
[07:15] Jordan: Any blockers from Redwood side?
[07:18] Alex (AE): Main dependency is your scripts and sample data plus network access if we run private. Also access to your eval metrics or the rubric for quality scoring.
[07:27] Priya (SRE): We'll need an NDA addendum for private infra access, and we'll send a signed copy.
[07:33] Alex (AE): Sounds good, we have an SLA and NDA pack; will send.
[07:37] Jordan: Ok, let's confirm next steps and owners.
[07:41] Alex (AE): I'll send the harness repo link, runbook, and security pack. Samir will take the integration and run plan. Jordan/Evan will provide two workload scripts (chat short-turn, long-context summary) and a 200-record sample dataset. Priya will coordinate network access and sign the NDA addendum.
[07:58] Maya (PM): Can we schedule the joint run for next Wednesday at 15:00 UTC?
[08:03] Alex (AE): Yes, tentative — we'll confirm after we get the assets.
[08:08] Samir (SE): Quick note: streaming tests often require lower client-side buffering. Please confirm your client uses chunked responses. Also we'll include a non-streaming baseline.
[08:21] Jordan: Sounds good. Anything else?
[08:25] Alex (AE): No, thanks all. We'll follow up in chat and send docs.

Notes: occasional transcription typos present (e.g., "KV cash" vs "KV cache", "Redwood Dedicatd"), some speaker labels simplified. Links shared in chat: benchmarking repo, security pack (links redacted in transcript).
